item.title: Lagrangian tori in the three-dimensional quadric and mirror symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.10108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the three-dimensional quadric, we study the Oakley--Usher torus and its Chekanov counterpart as defined by the authors in the companion paper \cite{OU1}. Computing the versal deformation of the $\Psi$-invariant of Shelukhin--Tonkonog--Vianna, we find that the Chekanov Oakley--Usher torus is knotted in a strong sense: it is not Hamiltonian isotopic to the Biran-lift of any Vianna torus in the two-dimensional quadric. Furthermore, we investigate enumerative properties of the Oakley--Usher torus in $Q^3$ and prove its non-displaceability, settling an open question asked by Oakley--Usher. We relate this to mirror symmetry by proving a split-generation result for the monotone Fukaya category of $Q^3$. This should be viewed as the analogue of a result by Abouzaid--Diogo after compactifying. Interestingly, in the compactification, the monotone copy of the $(S^1 \times S^2)$-generators of Abouzaid--Diogo becomes displaceable. On the other hand, the Oakley--Usher torus still appears as a generator. In the appendix joint with Soham Chanda, we give an alternative construction of the Chekanov Oakley--Usher torus using a double solid torus mutation. This allows us to compute its disk-potential using wall-crossing results.
item.dc:creator: Jo\'e Brendel, Andrea Piccirilli

item.title: Full fillings at the accumulation point and triangular limits of almost toric diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2611.10270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a closed symplectic four-manifold admitting an almost toric fibration over a disk. The ellipsoid embedding function of $M$ has an infinite staircase if it has infinitely many nonsmooth points. Cristofaro-Gardiner, Holm, Mandini, and Pires showed that these points must then accumulate at a solution of an explicit quadratic equation, and that at this accumulation point the ellipsoid embedding function agrees with the volume obstruction. We call this a full filling at the accumulation point, and study it in terms of almost toric fibrations. We show that if $M$ admits a sequence of almost toric base diagrams, each with a Delzant corner, converging nontrivially to a triangle, then $M$ has a full filling at its accumulation point. For the one-point blowups $H_b$ of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we also prove the converse. As a consequence, $H_b$ has an infinite staircase if and only if it admits such a sequence converging to a triangle whose hypotenuse has irrational slope.
item.dc:creator: Nicki Magill

item.title: An exact K\"ahler form on $(\mathbb C^*)^2$ without a global SYZ fibration
item.description: arXiv:2611.10532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an explicit exact K\"ahler form on \((\mathbb C^*)^2\) admitting no almost-toric fibration and hence no smooth Lagrangian torus fibration. For the logarithmic holomorphic volume form, we also rule out any special Lagrangian fibrations with compact fibers and dense regular locus, even when arbitrary compact connected singular fibers are allowed. For higher dimensions, taking products also yields explicit exact K\"ahler forms on \((\mathbb C^*)^n\), for every \(n\ge2\), admitting no smooth proper Lagrangian torus fibration.
item.dc:creator: Hang Yuan

item.title: On sinks and mirrors
item.description: arXiv:2611.11660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety. In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.
item.dc:creator: Mingyuan Hu, Vivek Shende

item.title: Cobordism maps and Atiyah-Floer isomorphisms for framed instanton homology I
item.description: arXiv:2611.10002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that isomorphisms of the type constructed by Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy, between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting, intertwine the cobordism maps of Kronheimer and Mrowka with maps defined by holomorphic curves alone, over the field of two elements. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc between its ends and an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. The symplectic maps count holomorphic triangles in moduli spaces of flat connections on surfaces, with the correspondence of a compression body as boundary condition for one- and three-handles. Consequently these maps are independent of the handle decomposition and of the Heegaard data, and form a functor isomorphic to framed instanton homology; where both are defined, our isomorphisms agree with those of Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy modulo two. The proof rests on two analytic results for the mixed anti-self-duality and holomorphic curve equation: an adiabatic limit in which a compression body collapses next to a holomorphic strip and becomes the Lagrangian boundary condition of its flat connections, and an excision theorem along a torus.
item.dc:creator: Bernd Johannes Wuebben

item.title: Liftable braid factorizations from line arrangements: Hironaka's relations and a Zariski pair
item.description: arXiv:2611.10328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We realize Hironaka's generalized lantern relations by lifting positive braid factorizations. For a nonpencil real line arrangement with no parallel lines, we construct a family of branched coverings on the regular fibers of a blown-up pencil of spheres. The motion of the branch points gives a factorization of a power of the full twist into least liftable powers of half-twists. The Artal-Carmona-Cogolludo-Marco Zariski pair gives two such factorizations of the same braid for a single simple branched covering of the disk. Their lifts are Hurwitz inequivalent even up to simultaneous conjugation by page homeomorphisms. The corresponding Milnor fibers fill the same planar contact three-manifold and have the same incidence matrix. They are homeomorphic and lie in distinct strong symplectic deformation classes.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Mori

item.title: Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.11171v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Gb$ be the group of germs of planar diffeomorphisms, fixing the origin, which preserve the standard b-symplectic form. The group acts on itself, under the usual left-right action and we identify, in the generic case, a simple representative of each orbit, depending on a non-vanishing, univariate, function. We then study the action of $\Gb$ on b-symplectic vector fields. For those fields that do not vanish at the origin, we establish a flow-box type theorem, while, for those that do vanish there, we show that the study of their conjugacy classes reduces to a classification of functions. We present this classification, when the origin is a regular point for these functions, while if it is a critical point, we present the orbits of their 2-jets. Finally, we address the problem of whether an element of $\Gb$ can be realised as the time-1 map of a b-symplectic vector field.
item.dc:creator: Stavros Anastassiou

item.title: Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.12751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all cluster models, compatibly with freezing, deleting, and contracting vertices of the quiver. This extends toric mirror symmetry and its naturalities beyond the cotangent bundle. In particular, we obtain homological mirror symmetry for all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties. We develop this package with a view towards conjectures of Marsh, Rietsch, and Williams about mirror symmetry for Grassmannians and closed positroid varieties. Motivated by these, we also conjecture that open positroid varieties are self-mirror. Assuming a natural ansatz, we prove this for a class of positroid varieties that includes nontrivial cells in every Grassmannian and all cells in finite-type Grassmannians. Towards this end we introduce a new combinatorial input, the notion of weak $k$-booleanness for permutations and braids.
item.dc:creator: Josephine Hlavinka

item.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations of Space Forms: Curvature Pinching, Soliton Rigidity, Conjugate Loci, and Superintegrability
item.description: arXiv:2611.12821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics $g_\lambda$ induced by the Hamiltonian cotangent deformation $H_\lambda = H_0 + \frac{\lambda}{2}\|J\|^2$ on simply connected space forms of constant curvature $\kappa \in \{1, 0, -1\}$, where $J$ is the momentum map of the isotropy action fixing a base point. The master reciprocal identity $1/f_\lambda^2 = 1/s_\kappa^2 + \lambda$ governing the warping function controls the geometry of the family and implies that radial geodesic acceleration is independent of $\lambda$. From this mechanism we derive three classes of results: (1) Curvature and rigidity: closed-form sectional curvatures, the sharp positivity trichotomy, pointwise and global Brendle-Schoen $1/4$-pinching windows on $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, never-Einstein rigidity for $\lambda \neq 0$, and the realization of Hamilton's steady cigar soliton on $(\mathbb{H}^2, g_1)$ as the unique gradient Ricci soliton in the family. (2) Dynamics and stability: iso-kinematic decoupling into unperturbed radial motion and uniform precession $\Omega = \lambda L$, closed-form Clairaut integration, the transcendental inward conjugate point law with Euclidean inversion $r_0 R^* = 1/\lambda$, and stratified $A_3$ cusp caustics. (3) Integrability and spectral theory: maximal superintegrable rational pericenter invariants on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, transverse Killing rigidity on curved space forms, Fuchsian Heun spectral reduction with modulus $\tau = 1 + \lambda/\kappa$, and essential spectrum gap collapse to $[0, \infty)$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$. Extensions to anisotropic sphere families and intrinsic deformations of compact rank-one symmetric spaces ($\mathbb{C}P^n, \mathbb{H}P^n, \mathbb{O}P^2$) are also established.
item.dc:creator: James J. Munden

item.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations and Closed-Form Geodesics on Non-Naturally Reductive Orbit Spheres: The Spin(9) 15-Sphere and the Cayley Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.12828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By the Skew-Torsion Holonomy Theorem of Olmos and Reggiani (2012), the 15-sphere $S^{15}$ admits no non-trivial naturally reductive metric under any transitive Lie group, precluding geodesic integration via canonical Ambrose-Singer connections. Simultaneously, Nikonorov (2013) established that every $Spin(9)$-invariant metric on $S^{15}$ is a geodesic orbit (GO) space. We integrate the geodesic flow on this non-naturally reductive GO manifold via the Lie Subalgebra Closure Principle: whenever the slice generators of a multi-axial reductive decomposition close into a finite-rank reductive Lie subalgebra, the geodesic vector equations decouple into an algebraic eigenvalue problem. Using the 16-dimensional spin representation and Vol'per's decomposition $\mathfrak{spin}(9) = \mathfrak{spin}(7) \oplus \mathfrak{p}_1 \oplus \mathfrak{p}_2$, we prove that the slice generators $X_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_2$ and $Y_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_1$ close into $\mathfrak{u}(2) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1) \subset \mathfrak{so}(16)$. The generator $M = \alpha X_1 + \beta Y_1$ has the four-mode spectrum $\Omega \in \{ |R \pm 3\alpha|, |R \pm \alpha| \}$ ($R = \sqrt{\alpha^2 + \beta^2}$), yielding a closed-form 4-projector decomposition and Euler-Cartan factorization for $\exp(\alpha X_1 + \beta Y_1)$. Under the normalized Ricci flow, we prove that the Bourguignon-Karcher squashed Einstein metric at $t = 3/11$ ($\lambda = 64$) is an unstable repeller separating sub-Riemannian fiber collapse from the round sphere basin. Finally, on the deformed Cayley plane $\mathbb{O}P^2 = F_4/Spin(9)$, we prove universal CROSS never-Einstein rigidity, establish the 15-dimensional three-stratum Whitney stratification of the cut locus $Cut(q_0)$ at non-polar basepoints $q_0$, and prove Blaschke and Besse rigidity for all $\lambda > 0$.
item.dc:creator: James J. Munden

item.title: Poisson cohomology of "book" Poisson structures
item.description: arXiv:2603.17277v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the Poisson cohomology of the linear Poisson structure dual to the n-dimensional "book" Lie algebra, defined by [e_0,e_i]=e_i, [e_i,e_j]=0, for i,j=1,...,n-1.
item.dc:creator: Henrique Bursztyn, Hudson Lima

item.title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08248v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period. On the infinitesimal side, the homotopy Poisson algebra of a connected admissible curve not contained in the degeneracy locus is $L_\infty$-isomorphic to its underlying cochain complex, and its $L_\infty$-isomorphism class is determined by the total contact multiplicity. The brackets of arity at least two can be removed by a change of tubular neighbourhood exactly when all contacts are transverse. At tangential contacts, the binary bracket retains the modular vector field. We establish this distinction using a general characterization of the $L_\infty$-isomorphisms induced by changes of tubular neighbourhood, valid for arbitrary coisotropic submanifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Ait Mohamed, Maxence Mayrand

item.title: Representation Varieties of Stacks and Trace Maps
item.description: arXiv:2609.09633v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define a derived stack $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ which generalizes the assignment $A\leadsto \operatorname{Rep}_n(A)$ to an algebra of its derived $GL_n$-representation variety of arXiv:1112.1449 from algebras $A$ to perfect stacks $X$ over characteristic 0 fields. In the case of a quasi-projective classical scheme $X$, we show that $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ admits a subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)\subset \mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$, which is in fact represented by a derived scheme almost of finite type. We further construct a Fourier-Mukai integral transform between the derived categories of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ and $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ which induces a trace map at the level of Hochschild homology generalizing the trace morphism constructed in arXiv:1112.1449 (for finitely presented commutative algebras). We show that the subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ is a derived enhancement of the framed locus of the Quot scheme of points and that this derived scheme is a $GL_n$-torsor over the stack of coherent length $n$ torsion sheaves. Hence, this stack is an analog of the derived character stack for quasi-projective schemes, and we show that for smooth, Calabi-Yau $X$, it inherits a shifted symplectic structure in the sense of arXiv:1111.3209 from the one constructed in arXiv:1812.11913 on the moduli stack of perfect complexes with proper support. This structure is shown to give a generalization of the classical symplectic structure on character varieties of surfaces of genus 1 constructed by Goldman \cite{gold}.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Erlikhman

item.title: Special Lagrangian cones in Deep Learning
item.description: arXiv:2609.20159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a matrix generalization of the cone of Harvey and Lawson and prove that it is an exact special Lagrangian manifold. We further show that it belongs to a family of exact special Lagrangian manifolds that foliate the balanced manifold arising in deep learning.
item.dc:creator: Tejas Kotwal, Govind Menon

item.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
item.description: arXiv:2610.41635v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.
item.dc:creator: Joseph T. A Peterson, Manoranjan Majji, John L. Junkins
